source_text: Εἶτα ὡς συναγαγὼν ἀραρυίαις ἀποδείξεσι καὶ ἀκολουθίαις τὸν λόγον εἶπε τό· καὶ ὅπερ ἔτι ἀτοπώτερον, αὐτὸς ὁ θεὸς τοῖς συντραπέζοις ἐπεβούλευε, προδότας καὶ δυσσεβεῖς ποιῶν. πῶς γὰρ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἢ ἐπεβούλευσεν ἢ προδότας καὶ δυσσεβεῖς τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐποίησεν, οὐκ ἂν ἔχοι παραδεικνύειν εἰ μὴ ἐξ ης ἐνόμισεν ἀκολουθίας. ἣν καὶ ὁ τυχὼν εὐχερέστατα διελέγξαι ἄν.
pass_a_gloss: Then, as having gathered together (συνάγω) the argument with fitted proofs (ἀποδείξεις) and consequences (ἀκολουθίαι), he said this: 'and what is still more absurd (ἀτοπώτερον), the god himself plotted against (ἐπιβουλεύω) the table-companions, making [them] traitors (προδόται) and irreverent (δυσσεβεῖς).' For how Jesus either plotted or made the disciples traitors and irreverent, he could not demonstrate except from the sequence/inference (ἀκολουθία) which he supposed (νομίζω); which even the chance person (ὁ τυχών) could most easily refute (διελέγχω).
pass_b_english: Then, as though he had drawn his argument together with tightly fitted proofs and logical steps, he said: “And, what is still more absurd, the god himself plotted against those at table with him, by making them traitors and impious men.” For he could not show how Jesus either plotted against his disciples or made them traitors and impious men, except from the chain of reasoning he imagined, which even an ordinary person could very easily refute.

choices.why: γάρ restored: 'But how ... he could not show' -> 'For he could not show how ...'

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; English is from the Greek.

Scripture citations sit inline beside the clause in Pass B.

translator_notes: Staged ης read as ἧς (relative). ὡς συναγαγὼν ἀραρυίαις ἀποδείξεσι is ironic (‘as though he had drawn his argument together with tightly fitted proofs’). θεός in Celsus’s quoted words rendered ‘the god’ (house convention). ‘Against his disciples’ makes explicit the object of ἐπεβούλευσεν, which is the same disciples named in the next clause; no new content added. No Scripture quoted.
